title: Weighted recovery of localized Airy fields
source_hypothesis: Actual CAA scalar-principal glancing system with arbitrary smooth complex lower matrices; either physical Airy sign; stable pair alpha=omega f0, v=omega f1 with compact precursor supports, fixed sufficiently small cone and large lower frequency, alpha in H5/6 and v in Hw. All source, input and output margins are fixed; coarse precursor norms are retained.
reviewed_arguments: The receiving domain is the actual stable pair alpha=omega f0, v=omega f1 with compact precursor supports, alpha in H5/6 and v in Hw. It is not declared to contain every energy solution.
Both scalar signs retain the same complex matrix amplitudes and the exact pi-normalized decomposition of the stable norm.

Exact outgoing negative-ray phase extraction and positive-ray decay give all amplitude derivatives across the transition. The smoothed phase has a uniformly small gradient and higher derivatives with positive decay order.

Full nonstationary integrations prove every off-displacement kernel derivative, rapid output decay and all coarse-to-strong Sobolev estimates. Frequency-cutoff boundary terms are controlled in the oscillatory limit.
One fixed larger input cutoff contains all displaced singularities. The common extraction is applied in its original operator order; only afterwards are the fully smooth tails restored.
Interior recovery controls alpha and Z_epsilon v in H5/6 with arbitrary finite coarse precursor norms. No exponentially growing inverse multiplier or unsupported cutoff commutation is used.
The actual boundary row is inverted on nested patches with the whole graph remainder. Noncompact tails and angular leakage retain explicit coarse bounds.
The variable-coefficient weak-domain trace theorem is applied before subtracting the decaying Airy trace. This recovers v in the boundary-layer space without an unproved trace regularity assumption.
The exact sum of weight contributions yields the complete weighted reverse estimate on the stated construction range for arbitrary smooth complex lower matrices.

Rapid equation-error amplitudes give all required coarse source bounds by explicit Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz. The differentiated outer output-cutoff error is retained and lies outside the source observation.

The forward and reverse inequalities hold directly on the completed weighted domain. Frequency truncation is not assumed to preserve compact precursor support. Field-error dependence remains quantitative.
Three solved exercises give the full input displacement, exact weight constants and a counterexample to inferring surjectivity from two norm estimates.
Twenty-seven exact symbolic checks, 210 formulas, 24 displays, nine overlapping desktop captures, the entire figure and two mobile samples were checked and actually inspected.

The full weighted range estimate is proved; arbitrary-solution representation, residual matching and general manifold scalar observation assembly remain active. The 92 required human foundation proofs remain external.
